name: json_schema_validate

parameters.name: schema
parameters.description: The [JSON Schema](https://json-schema.org/) document to validate against. The DuckDB 2.0 build supports drafts 4, 6, 7, 2019-09 and 2020-12, selected by `$schema` (2020-12 when absent); an unknown `$schema` is an error. The Haybarn 1.5 build targets [draft-07](https://json-schema.org/draft-07/json-schema-release-notes) only.

parameters.name: json_data
parameters.description: The JSON value to validate. Pass a column of type `JSON`, a struct literal, or a string cast with `::JSON`.

returns: BOOLEAN — TRUE for conforming data; raises an error for nonconforming data or an invalid schema. SQL NULL inputs propagate NULL.
description: Validate a JSON value against a JSON Schema. Validation failures raise an error; they do not return FALSE. In the DuckDB 2.0 build the error names up to five failing locations (as JSON Pointers) without echoing the document; use [`json_schema_is_valid`](#json_schema_is_valid) for a boolean result and [`json_schema_errors`](#json_schema_errors) for a structured report. On the Haybarn 1.5 build, use COALESCE(TRY(json_schema_validate(schema, payload)), false) for row filtering, after validating the schema separately (TRY also catches malformed-schema errors).

examples.description: Filter a column on schema conformance

name: json_schema_is_valid

parameters.name: schema
parameters.description: The [JSON Schema](https://json-schema.org/) document. The DuckDB 2.0 build supports drafts 4, 6, 7, 2019-09 and 2020-12, selected by `$schema` (2020-12 when absent); an unknown `$schema` is an error. An invalid schema raises an error.

parameters.name: json_data
parameters.description: The JSON value to check. Pass a column of type `JSON`, a struct literal, or a string cast with `::JSON`.

returns: BOOLEAN — TRUE for conforming data, FALSE otherwise; raises an error only for an invalid schema. SQL NULL inputs propagate NULL.
description: Return whether a JSON value conforms to a JSON Schema. Unlike [`json_schema_validate`](#json_schema_validate) a nonconforming document returns FALSE instead of raising, so it can be used directly in `WHERE` and `FILTER` clauses without `TRY`; an invalid schema still raises an error, so a broken contract is never mistaken for bad data. New in the DuckDB 2.0 build.

examples.description: 2020-12 keywords such as prefixItems are enforced

examples.code:
SELECT
  COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE     json_schema_is_valid('{"type":"object","properties":{"id":{"type":"integer"}},"required":["id"]}', payload)) AS valid,
  COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE NOT json_schema_is_valid('{"type":"object","properties":{"id":{"type":"integer"}},"required":["id"]}', payload)) AS invalid
FROM events;

name: json_schema_errors
returnType: STRUCT(path VARCHAR, keyword VARCHAR, message VARCHAR)[]

parameters.name: schema
parameters.description: The [JSON Schema](https://json-schema.org/) document. The DuckDB 2.0 build supports drafts 4, 6, 7, 2019-09 and 2020-12, selected by `$schema` (2020-12 when absent); an unknown `$schema` is an error. An invalid schema raises an error.

parameters.name: json_data
parameters.description: The JSON value to check. Pass a column of type `JSON`, a struct literal, or a string cast with `::JSON`.

returns: LIST(STRUCT(path VARCHAR, keyword VARCHAR, message VARCHAR)) — one entry per validation error, empty for a conforming document. `path` is a JSON Pointer into the document (empty string for the root). SQL NULL inputs propagate NULL.
description: Return every validation error of a JSON value against a JSON Schema as a structured list: where in the document it failed (`path`), which schema keyword failed (`keyword`) and a readable `message`. Use it to build data-quality reports or quarantine tables that record why each row was rejected. An invalid schema raises an error. New in the DuckDB 2.0 build.

examples.description: List the errors of one document

examples.code:
SELECT row_num, e.path, e.keyword, e.message
FROM events,
     unnest(json_schema_errors('{"type":"object","properties":{"id":{"type":"integer"}},"required":["id"]}', payload)) AS t(e)
ORDER BY row_num;

name: json_schema_validate_schema

parameters.name: schema
parameters.description: Candidate JSON Schema. The function compiles it, which catches malformed JSON, unsupported `$schema` drafts, invalid regular expressions and unresolvable `$ref`s; it is not exhaustive validation against the JSON Schema meta-schema.

returns: BOOLEAN — TRUE if the schema is accepted; raises an error if it is invalid. SQL NULL propagates NULL.
description: Check that a JSON Schema compiles. An invalid schema raises an error, making this useful as a deployment gate. Use COALESCE(TRY(json_schema_validate_schema(definition)), false) when auditing a registry and you want invalid entries flagged instead of aborting the query. Compiling is not exhaustive meta-schema validation; some misspelled keywords are simply ignored, as the JSON Schema specification requires.

examples.description: Find any malformed schemas in a registry table

name: json_schema_patch

parameters.name: schema
parameters.description: [JSON Schema](https://json-schema.org/) document. Properties whose `default` keyword is set are the ones that contribute to the patch.

parameters.name: json_data
parameters.description: The (possibly incomplete) JSON value. Missing properties for which the schema declares a `default` will appear in the resulting patch.

returns: JSON — a [JSON Patch (RFC 6902)](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc6902) array of `add` operations that, when applied, fill in the missing defaults.
description:
Compute the JSON Patch (RFC 6902) diff that would bring `json_data` into conformance with the `default` values declared by the schema. Returns the patch — does **not** apply it (use `json_schema_update` for the in-place variant).

Use the patch when you want to log or audit which fields were synthesized, or when you need to apply the same diff to multiple downstream representations of the document. The function also validates the document and raises on invalid values; defaults do not repair type mismatches. Use TRY for an audit column that should return NULL on errors, and validate the schema separately first.

examples.description: Generate a patch for a partial document
Audit patches; NULL marks input or schema errors

name: json_schema_update

parameters.name: schema
parameters.description: [JSON Schema](https://json-schema.org/) document. Properties with `default` declared are filled in where the input is missing them.

parameters.name: json_data
parameters.description: The JSON value to enrich. Existing fields are preserved; only missing properties with declared `default` values are added.

returns: JSON — the input value with missing defaults filled in.
description:
Apply the schema's `default` values inline. Equivalent to running `json_schema_patch` and applying the resulting patch — but in a single function call you can use directly in a `SELECT` projection.

This is the function to reach for when you want enriched JSON, not a diff. The function also validates the document and raises on invalid values; defaults do not repair type mismatches. Use TRY for an audit column that should return NULL on errors, and validate the schema separately first.

examples.description: Build a clean table with defaults applied
